Users who deposit $10 receive $20 in trading credits. What do motor sports odds mean?When it comes to motorsports and racing markets, odds are displayed and read similarly to how they are for most sports. Let's say a driver is priced at -150 to win the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7th, and the next best driver has +200 odds. That means the driver at -150 is a decent favorite to win, and you'd have to risk $150 to win $100. The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.Outright/To Win oddsThis market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.As of August 24, 2026, here are the latest odds to win the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Championship, per DraftKings Sportsbook:Denny Hamlin +100Ryan Blaney +550Christopher Bell +750Tyler Reddick +750Ty Gibbs +850IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event.         WNBA veteran DeWanna Bonner has agreed to a buyout with the Phoenix Mercury, giving the six-time All-Star a chance to compete for a championship in what could potentially be her last season in the league. The question now is where could the 39-year-old finish her accomplished career?Bonner already won two titles in 2009 and 2014, both with Phoenix. Besides four years with Connecticut and part of a season with the Fever, she has mostly been part of the Mercury. In her 17th WNBA season, the 6-foot-4 wing is averaging 10.6 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. She is a versatile, dynamic scorer and an elite rebounder, ranking in the top five for most career rebounds in league history.The timing of the buyout was not by chance. Monday was the deadline for player playoff eligibility from waivers. Because Bonner was waived by Monday, she is eligible to play in the playoffs with another team. Any player waived after Monday could sign with another team for the remainder of the regular season, but could not participate in the playoffs. The Mercury (13-24) have also officially been eliminated from the playoffs, so this gives Bonner a chance to go out on top if she is planning to retire after this season
"Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason," said Phoenix General Manager Nick U'ren in an official statement. title: Dana Brown out as Astros GM; owner Jim Crane to oversee baseball operations - CBS Sports
description: The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
body:
The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Houston Astros and general manager Dana Brown have mutually agreed to part ways, the team announced Monday morning.Owner Jim Crane will oversee baseball operations "through the transition period," according to the team. Brown's responsibilities will be divided among the assistant general managers -- Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff -- and senior advisor Jeff Bagwell, the Hall of Fame first baseman who spent his entire 15-year playing career with Houston."Over the past four seasons, Dana has helped our organization win two division titles and has led our baseball front office through key scouting, draft and development efforts," Crane said in a statement. "On behalf of the Astros, I want to thank him for his commitment, energy, and contributions to our organization. We wish he and his family the best."
        
            
                Seven more MLB executives who could be on the hot seat after Astros' Dana Brown
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Brown took over the front office heading into the 2023 season, taking the helm of the defending World Series champions. The Astros won the AL West in 2023 and 2024 and advanced all the way to the ALCS in 2023. Last season, however, they missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016, and Brown entered this season as a lame duck. 
The Astros are currently tied for first place in the AL West, but sit one game under .500 at 65-66."I want to thank Jim Crane for the opportunity to serve in my first role as an MLB general manager," Brown said in a statement. "The Astros organization and the fans have welcomed me and my family, and I am grateful to have called Houston home for the past four seasons. I wish the organization well and I look forward to the future as I continue my 36-plus years in professional baseball."Manager Joe Espada, who is also working out the final year of his contract, has not had any "conversations about his future," according to The Athletic.
Brown, 59, played college ball for Seton Hall before being a 35th round draft pick and spending three years in the minors. Immediately after his playing days were concluded, he became a minor-league coach and then a scout. He worked his way up the chain for years in front offices, becoming vice president of scouting for the Braves in 2019. The Astros GM job was his first as the top decision-maker. Crane has been the Astros' owner since 2011. On his watch, the Astros became a powerhouse, making the playoffs eight straight seasons -- a run that includes seven division titles, four pennants and two World Series championships. Jeff Luhnow was the general manager from 2011-19, but was dismissed after the sign stealing scandal. James Click was the GM from 2020-22 and Brown took over after that.Now, with the playoffs still in sight, the Astros will be looking for a new lead executive.
Inside the 2026 seasonIt's been an interesting run for the Astros this year. As noted, they are tied for first place, albeit with a sub-.500 record.On the good side, Yordan Alvarez has put it all together -- and stayed healthy -- and is having an MVP campaign. He enters the last week of August leading the majors in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS, OPS+ and total bases, while also leading the American League in average, home runs, RBI and walks. He's slashing .320/.436/.613 with 36 homers and 90 RBI. Pitching has been an issue. The Astros rank 25th in baseball with a 4.63 staff ERA. The rotation has actually been a disaster, as the Astros are 28th in the majors with a 5.15 ERA from starting pitchers. Their big free-agent signing was Tatsuya Imai, who has lost his spot in the rotation while sporting a 5.32 ERA. 
Curiously, the Astros added just center fielder Daulton Varsho in front of the trade deadline, when it was pretty obvious they needed rotation help.Regardless, the Astros got hot in late July -- winning 11 of 12 at one point -- and that's enough to be relevant in the AL West.

title: Deshaun Watson contract: Why Browns will cut QB in 2027 - CBS Sports
description: Cleveland is turning to Watson now even though his contract makes it almost impossible for him to remain with the
body:
Cleveland is turning to Watson now even though his contract makes it almost impossible for him to remain with the team beyond this year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Cleveland Browns officially have a starting quarterback in Deshaun Watson, and for some reason, they decided to give the job to a player who likely doesn't have a future with the team.Due to the way Watson's contract is structured, the Browns will almost certainly release him in March, and that just adds another bizarre layer to the team's decision to hand him the starting QB job. The Browns could have given the job to Shedeur Sanders, but instead, they gave it to someone who essentially has no future in Cleveland.The $200 million reason why Deshaun Watson will be gone after the 2026 seasonAfter the Browns traded for Watson in 2022, they gave him a five-year, $230 million contract that was fully guaranteed. Not only did the Browns make one of the worst trades in NFL history, but they followed it up by handing out one of the worst contracts ever. That's the kind of double whammy that can set your team back for the better part of a decade.Over the past four years, the Browns have restructured Watson's contract multiple times, mainly so Cleveland could kick the can down the road on his salary cap hits. However, the Browns also included a poison pill when they restructured his contract in December 2024, and the clause pretty much guarantees they will cut Watson by March 13, 2027, so be sure to mark your calendar, Browns fans.
Here's how the clause works, via former NFL agent Joel Corry, who laid out the details in February:During the restructure, Watson had two dummy/voiding years in 2027 and 2028 that were turned into real contract years with minimum salaries. Watson also has a base salary of $200 million in 2029 that's NOT guaranteed, but it becomes FULLY guaranteed if he's still on the roster by the third day of the league year in 2027. If the Browns don't want to pay the $200 million, they have to cut Watson before March 13, 2027. (This is a team that once had a trade fall through because they forgot to file the paperwork with the NFL, so hopefully someone sets an alarm for March 12 so they remember to cut Watson.)By the time next March rolls around, the Browns will have paid Watson $230 million, and you can go ahead and bet everything you own that they're going to make sure they don't have to pay him another dollar.If Watson were to somehow lead the Browns to the Super Bowl this year, the team would still be forced to cut him because there's no way they'd be able to afford to keep him with the $200 million salary becoming guaranteed in 2029. 
And that's the issue here: If Watson plays well, he has no future with the team. If he doesn't play well, he has no future with the team. Starting Sanders would have made more sense.
        
            
                Browns fans, keep booing: Todd Monken picking Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders is wrong, even if it's right
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Although the Browns will avoid paying Watson $200 million by releasing him, they will have to take a massive $86.2 million dead cap hit, which will go down as the second-largest in NFL history. The NFL record for the largest dead cap hit was set just a few months ago when the Miami Dolphins took on a $99.2 million hit when they released Tua Tagovailoa.The Dolphins are taking on that dead cap hit over two seasons, and that's almost certainly what the Browns will do once they release Watson. The Browns will be able to designate him as a post-June 1 release, allowing them to divide the cap hit over 2027 and 2028:
2027: $34.7 million in dead cap2028: $51.5 million in dead capThe Browns' decision to acquire Watson has been a nightmare since the day it happened, but by 2028, they'll finally be able to put the entire ordeal behind them. Through four seasons, Watson has made $184 million for 19 starts, and he's gone 9-10 in those starts. Yes, that means the Browns have paid him $20.4 million per win. That's good work if you can get it.The Browns will pay Watson $46 million more in 2026, and that will likely be the last time they give him a single penny.

title: Ole Miss had FBI sweep for bugs after Lane Kiffin left for LSU, NIL director claims - CBS Sports
description: The paranoia was at an all-time high in Oxford after Kiffin left town
body:
The paranoia was at an all-time high in Oxford after Kiffin left town
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:31 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Paranoia inside the Ole Miss football facility following Lane Kiffin's messy departure to LSU last season was not manufactured. Walker Jones, the executive director of the Grove Collective at Ole Miss, revealed the Rebels went to extreme lengths to ensure no tampering or espionage was involved."We actually had the FBI come through and walk the building for bugs and for everything," Jones said on the Assorted Crackers podcast. "We knew kind of what was in Baton Rouge, and we knew how they operated. I remember getting on my knees and looking underneath desks and seeing if there was some sort of bug involved. Somebody was like, 'What are you doing?' and I was like, 'Trust me, you don't know this guy (Kiffin) like I do.'"That detail sounds more appropriate for a political thriller than a coaching change, but it illustrates how seriously the Rebels viewed the possibility of internal sabotage.The paranoia was real, widespread, and unlike anything the program had experienced during the modern coaching carousel. There was legitimate concern Kiffin might leave behind trusted assistants as de facto spies, using their continued access to players and staffers to help coax key pieces of the roster toward Baton Rouge.
That fear shaped nearly every decision during a volatile transition. Ole Miss officials questioned loyalties, monitored communication and tried to determine which assistants were committed to the Rebels and which remained connected to Kiffin. In the transfer portal era, where one conversation can trigger a roster exodus, even a hint of divided allegiance was treated as an immediate threat.Jones said he spent "several nights" sleeping at the Manning Center in an effort to retain most of the Rebels' roster.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin's pursuit of ex-NFL TE Dae'Quan Wright is latest example of LSU coach not caring what you think
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"What people don't realize is half the staff was going to LSU," Jones said. "We had to have two different text threads, two different staff meetings, we had to ask coaches to leave the room, we had no hall room conversations, nothing written on the grease boards in the office, because we were going to be competing against (half the staff for players)."
Kiffin's exit was never going to be clean, given his relationships inside the building and LSU's ability to pursue Ole Miss players. What followed was a Cold War atmosphere in Oxford, complete with suspected double agents, heightened security and the belief that every conversation could impact the roster.LSU would end up prying away only a couple of the Rebels' top players, like Princewill Umanmielen and TJ Dottery, but was unsuccessful in reported attempts to seize Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy. The Tigers signed this 2026 cycle's top-rated portal class to complete a roster that exceeds $40 million in payroll.LSU plays Ole Miss on Sept. 19The Tigers come to Oxford early this season in what's expected to be a rude welcome for Kiffin. 
Ole Miss fans do not hate Kiffin because he left -- they hate how he left. After building the Rebels into a national contender, Kiffin bolted for LSU during the most important stretch of the season, turning a potential championship run into a public spectacle centered on his future. The timing felt calculated, the messaging came across as disingenuous, and the fallout created the immediate fears of roster tampering, according to Jones. Ole Miss supporters believed Kiffin treated Oxford like a stepping stone after insisting the program could compete with anyone. Leaving for an SEC rival was betrayal enough. Trying to bring players and staffers with him made it personal.
While he's focused on his new job with bringing LSU another national championship, Kiffin said last month that both programs came out well."In a lot of ways, a lot of people won," Kiffin said at SEC media days. "A lot of coaches either stayed or came. They were able to keep Pete Golding as a head coach, so he became a head coach. Players got a lot of really big contracts in both places. Assistant coaches did in both places. Both are talked about a lot as premier programs heading into next year."It's hard to imagine Ole Miss supporters feeling the same.

        As the calendar enters the final third of the schedule for the 2026 NWSL regular season, it's no surprise players are still producing big moments. Whether it's on the pitch or off, it's time to roll out Attacking Third's NWSL Team of the Week honors.Everyone's favorite content trend is back for another season. After weekly matches across the 2026 NWSL season, Attacking Third analysts will select a team of the week, head coach, and honorary captain based on performances across the weekend.Here you can find a mix of stats and data, analysis from our pundits, and highlights you may have missed over the weekend. If you're keeping track of who earned past honors, check out our previous team of the week.This week, we had a bit more fun, even changed up our preferred lineup formation, and saluted an NWSL legend. Coaches made history too, so congratulations to Karina Baez on becoming the first-ever Mexican woman to earn a regular-season win in a head coaching role. 
Here's who made the latest edition:
Goalkeeper: Jordan Silkowitz (Bay FC)Jordan Silkowitz has put her goalkeeper skills on display all year for Bay FC. Her 85 saves through 19 games this season lead the entire league, and while it's a stat that can sometimes say more about the team's entire defensive state, it's still impressive. This week she's on the team for another shot-stopping clinic against Houston Dash.
Defender: Rafaelle (Orlando Pride)Orlando have to scrap their way out of a slump, and that oftentimes starts out back. Pride defender and Brazilian international Rafaelle was non-stop in providing defensive coverage against Washington Spirit. She led the team in shot blocks (three) and clearances (18).Defender: Jayden Perry (Portland Thorns FC)Sometimes the defensive play that helps the most is the ones that come when you're capable of controlling the ball and aiding in distribution and that's what Thorns FC fullback Jayden Perry did over the weekend. She helped Portland pick up their first clean sheet since July 5. 
Defender: Sarah Gorden (Angel City)Angel City defender Sarah Gorden is a league veteran and knows how to produce big moments when the team needs it. She picked up two critical blocks against Gotham FC to disrupt any link-ups between Sam Kerr and Jaedyn Shaw.
Midfielder: Lauren Milliet (Racing Louisville) A double match week for Louisville and Lauren Milliet's three assists over two games put her into the team as we tweak our lineup a bit. She delivered a heads-up assist off a short throw-in.
Midfielder: Jessie Fleming (Portland Thorns)Portland Thorns midfielder Jessie Fleming showed off her vision and line-breaking pass ability with this long ball through to find Sophia Wilson for a goal.
Midfielder: Haley McCutcheon (Orlando Pride)Barbra Banda is back, and Pride midfielder Haley McCutcheon welcomed her back by getting a foot on this great pass for the game winner against Washington Spirit.
Midfielder: Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars FC)Welcome back to the team, Mallory Swanson. This week it's for her skillful spin-in-the-box goal and an epic call-your-shot assist to Jameese Joseph. 
Forward: Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage)There's a new leader in the NWSL Golden Boot race, and it's North Carolina Courage winger Ashley Sanchez. She doesn't look like she'll stop scoring anytime soon. 
Forward: Trinity Byars (San Diego Wave FC)San Diego have been on the hunt for goals several weeks now, and thankfully, Trinity Byars is the answer. Two goals and an assist for team of the week honors, and what a sprint for this go-ahead goal.
Forward: Kat Rader (Houston Dash)Midweek games can feel like forever ago, but they still count for team of the week memories. Rookie Kat Rader is having a good season for the Dash and can't stop scoring. 
Coach: Karina Baez (Chicago Stars FC)After a head coaching change, a shift in staff, and one draw later, the Chicago Stars finally got a win for interim head coach Karina Baez. A 3-2 win over Racing Louisville, which ended their four-game win streak, finally brought some joy to the lakefront for Chicago. A historic one too: Karina Baez becomes the first-ever Mexican woman to win an NWSL game in a head coaching role. 
Honorary captain: Tobin Heath (Portland Thorns)For a brief moment, all was right in the NWSL universe because Tobin Heath was able to sign a one-day contract and officially retire as a Portland Thorns player. The U.S. Soccer Hall of Famer, two-time World Cup winner, Olympic gold medalist, and all-around certified baller was just as decorated in league play. She's the club's all-time assist leader (66) and won two NWSL Championships (2013, 2017) and the NWSL Shield (2016). She held the all-time single-season assist record (10) for nearly a decade before Croix Bethune matched the 10 assists in 2024. Her number is now retired in Portland, but her legacy is forever.

The opening round of Premier League fixtures offered plenty of surprises, making for a fitting set-up for what is expected to be an unpredictable season in England

        For a Premier League season that boasted a reputation for unpredictability before a ball was kicked, the opening round of fixtures marked a fitting way to begin the new campaign.While a few results went exactly as expected, the weekend's games offered example after example of teams in transition and limited proof of concept along the way. It does not come as all that much of a surprise – nine teams entered the season with new coaches while others began a first full campaign in charge after joining their teams midseason, while squad overhaul and the jump from the Championship to the Premier League mean settling into things is easier said than done. Some of the teams with new looks will likely be fine in the long run but they will first have to navigate the uncertainties that come with fresh starts, making most of the teams in the league a genuine work in progress at this very early juncture of the campaign.It should come as no surprise, then, that the teams for whom consistency is a defining feature impressed – the unpredictability surrounding the most notable clubs actually means there's an opportunity for the rest to climb up the ranks. The first weekend, though, serves as a fascinating benchmark for all and makes for the first benchmark for just about every team on the table. Those who punched above their weight will be tasked with keeping it up as the season progresses, while those with room for improvement still have plenty of time to actually make the necessary changes to get where they want to be.Here's the first batch of many power rankings this season in the Premier League.1. ArsenalThere is nothing particularly noteworthy about beating a newly promoted team 3-0 but in Arsenal's case, no news is good news. This is a team that is fully comfortable and confident in their identity, unsurprisingly living up to the billing as the team to beat for the title.
2. Brighton and Hove AlbionThe storyline of the weekend are the midtable teams whose consistency is their strength, Brighton and Hove Albion leading the pack. It is one thing to get the better of Aston Villa post-mass exodus but Brighton drove the point home with a 4-0 drubbing, scoring all of their goals by the 31st minute and going into cruise control from there.3. BrentfordBrighton's win over Villa was tonally similar to Brentford's 3-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur, a game of two teams with very contrasting looks. The Bees played with a clear identity and no problem executing their game plan, Igor Thiago's missed penalty the only low point in an otherwise perfect display.4. ChelseaChelsea may have been a bit more leaky at the back than they would have liked in their 3-2 win over Fulham but the underlying statistics show a much more commanding win than the scoreline reflects. It's early days but Cole Palmer's goal and assist offer some reassurance that his uptick in form will align with his team's.
5. Manchester UnitedSure, Manchester City spent much of the game down a goal to Bournemouth but they had solidly outplayed the Cherries over the course of 90 minutes and their eventual 2-1 win was a natural reflection of things. They lacked some urgency in the first half but their ability to grow into the game is a source of optimism as Enzo Maresca settles into his new role on the touchline.6. LiverpoolIt will take more than one game for new coach Andoni Iraola to solve Liverpool's tactical imbalance – their talented attack is still being canceled out by a vulnerable defense, which is why they had to settle for a point at Newcastle United. The makings of a decent defensive shape are there and the attack might be enough to push them over the line when needed, though they might be resigned to inconsistency without some notable roster changes.7. Crystal PalaceCrystal Palace may have lost 2-0 to Everton but they dictated the tempo of the game and outdid the Toffees in expected goals by a margin of 1.96 to 1.12 despite taking five fewer shots. There's an argument to be made that Palace will put all the pieces together sooner rather than later, their first performance under new coach Pierre Sage more encouraging than not.
8. EvertonThere's always a certain value in midtable teams picking up wins against the opponents that, like them, are destined to sit somewhere in the middle of the pack by season's end. A weird weekend, though, means the Toffees get to enjoy a decent spot in the power rankings despite the argument that Crystal Palace may have outplayed them in their 2-0 win.9. Newcastle UnitedNewcastle United are not the team that they were two years ago – high-profile names like Alexander Isak and Anthony Gordon are elsewhere, and a coaching change midway through preseason means expectations can only be so high for them. The Magpies, though, deserve credit for taking advantage of Liverpool's vulnerabilities and nearly sneaking out a win from their 2-2 draw this weekend.10. Ipswich TownFor the most part, the newly promoted teams enjoyed a pleasant return to the Premier League, with Ipswich Town easily the most impressive. The one thing every relegation-challenged team needs to do is take points off of the teams they will likely be battling to stay out of the bottom three and Ipswich very much outplayed Sunderland to start the season on a high.
11. FulhamFulham may not have done enough just yet to assuage fears that they will be locked in a relegation battle this season but in a weekend defined by average-to-genuinely-bad showings from a batch of teams, the Cottagers did just enough to land in the middle of the pack.  12. BournemouthBournemouth will feel hard done by after their loss at City, conceding two late goals to see a 1-0 lead slip away. They played with a bit of naivete down the stretch that some might find concerning, but it's a fixable problem as they begin to settle into life with new coach Marco Rose, so there's no need to panic right now.13. Hull CityHull City's luck has not run out just yet. They were not exactly the better team against Manchester United but were resourceful on set pieces and benefitted from an opponent that lacked spark in attack despite their efforts. Plus, they and Ipswich are already off to a better start than last season's 20th-place team, Wolverhampton Wanderers – they did not win their first game until the festive fixtures came around.
14. Leeds UnitedLike Ipswich Town, Leeds United did what they needed to do in picking up a valuable win over Nottingham Forest. That is where the compliments begin and end, though – they may have limited Forest to just 0.66 expected goals and two shots on target but Leeds only generated 0.47 xG of their own, which is far from impressive.15. Nottingham ForestEven if Nottingham Forest generated a bit more in attack than Leeds United did, they really did not do enough to pick up a moral victory along the way.16. Manchester UnitedA notable selection of teams underperformed in their opening games of the season, Manchester United among them. They may have outshot Hull City 21 to eight but looked pretty unimpressive in terms of end product, a signal that they do not have it all figured out just yet – and that their set piece defending could use some work.
17. Tottenham HotspurBrentford's excellent day came at Tottenham Hotspur's expense, a team that looked like they lacked a cohesive identity despite weeks of preseason work with Roberto De Zerbi in his first full season in the gig. It was almost the most unimpressive showing of the weekend but Spurs were missing a few key players that might fix a bunch of their problems so they might be able to put this behind them quickly enough.18. Coventry CityCoventry City were the promoted side people had the highest hopes for … and were also the only newly promoted side that did not win this weekend. A demolition by Arsenal does not change perceptions about them all that much but the fact that they took just one shot on target is not encouraging, especially since they will spend the early stretch of the season without the injured Haji Wright.19. SunderlandA judgment call based on one game seems harsh but it already feels like Sunderland's plan to reboot last season's lucky approach may be an unwise one. They were fully outplayed by a newly promoted team in Ipswich Town that many believe will drop straight down to the Championship, which is as disappointing an outing as one can muster.
20. Aston VillaIt was an unpleasant weekend for several teams but no one underwhelmed more than Aston Villa, who were already 4-0 down by the 31st minute and down a player before halftime. Their preseason bet that they would survive a mass exodus with young, new signings did not pay off in the slightest and if their loss to Brighton and Hove Albion is anything to go by, they are in for a rough season.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a number of different wagering options available on each race, and here we will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that help clarify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports. That is because racetracks use parimutuel wagering.                      Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll be paid out at are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is an even more conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           You can also combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available to those interested, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does in other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will even allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses is 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and just two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           These are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to an unsustainable early pace.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and having more space. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

title: Three Fantasy Football sleepers Jacob Gibbs can't stop drafting - CBS Sports
description: Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his rost
body:
Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his roster
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:13 pm ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        I wrote up Jonathon Brooks in this morning's newsletter. Here's a link, if you missed that. My favorite sleepers this off-season have been Brooks, Josh Downs, and Jayden Reed. Brooks is no longer a sleeper. Downs and Reed still are! I write about them all of the time, though. You can read about those two here. So let's transition to three players the Fantasy Football community and more importantly your home league drafts are still probably sleeping on!Sleeper #1 - Jaylin Noel, WR, Houston TexansJaylin Noel was a very good prospect. In my opinion, he was one of the biggest steals of the 2025 NFL Draft. The Texans landed him in Round 4.His game translated right away as a rookie. He was a great returner. Noel also won down the field, and he won as a pre-snap motion threat on out-breaking routes. He is great tracking the ball, has reliable hands, and is a springy athlete who can create separation.According to Matt Harmon's Reception Perception charting, Noel fell in exclusive company in terms of grading out 70th percentile or better vs. man, press, and zone coverage in 2025. He's free in drafts. The Texans traded for Kayshon Boutte, but a late-August add leads to a ramp-up period to learn the scheme and get on the same page as C.J. Stroud in the passing game. 
Sleeper #2 - Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver BroncosDenver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is not free in drafts, but I do believe he is underrated. He's the Denver Broncos RB who I have ranked the highest. The opening schedule for the Broncos is pretty rough. The second half of the season looks nice, on paper.I expect Coleman to play a role on passing downs (and potentially in short-yardage situations) right away for the Broncos. I was extremely impressed with his college film, particularly in pass protection. The Broncos felt the same way. Sean Payton said, "That was a strong suit when you were looking at his tape -- different than the rest of the class," in reference to Coleman's pass protection.If there's an injury in the backfield, Coleman has a three-down skill set. He's ready to step into a bell-cow role in a top-half-of-the-league offense. And I really do think there's a lot to like about his tape as a runner. His rushing efficiency was up-and-down in college, and many view him as a plodder because he's a little buff boi. There were flashes of tempo, block-setting, and decent burst early in the 2025 season from Coleman, before he got banged-up and his offensive line struggled to close out the season. If he's a better rusher than many expect, Coleman might not need an injury to carve out a Fantasy-friendly role for himself in this backfield.
He's a bit more expensive than some of my favorite upside bench stashes -- Demond Claiborne, Emmett Johnson, Kaelon Black, and Adam Randall -- but I do view Coleman as worth a Round 10 draft pick if in need of bench RB upside.Sleeper #3 - Cyrus Allen, WR, Kansas City ChiefsI'm buying the Cyrus Allen hype. Why wouldn't we? He was productive in college, and his film backed it up. The ways he won feel sustainable. It wasn't schemed-up college nonsense. It wasn't picking on poor competition. He was winning routes. He was winning at the catch point. He has a good feel for space and was consistently presenting an open target vs. zone coverage.The drumbeat coming out of Chiefs training camp has been loud and consistent. Allen looked great in the first preseason game. Everything points towards this being a talented player who was overlooked in the NFL Draft. It happens every year.
Allen feels a bit buried on the depth chart (no surprise, we're talking about a rookie WR in August), but let's not pretend as if this Chiefs receiver room has any stalwarts on it. This is as inconsistent of a WR room as we are going to find in the NFL (Dolphins always excluded from this type of discussion). Any or all three of the Chiefs top receivers could miss time. Or Allen could just prove to be the best one. Check out the Rashee Rice Reception Perception profile. The Chiefs don't have a consistent separator. Or, they have not had one. Maybe they do now!

title: LSU expected to add ex-Ole Miss star DT Zxavian Harris after NFL stint - CBS Sports
description: Lane Kiffin hasn't been shy about bringing NFL rookies back into the fold, as another former Ole Miss star is exp
body:
Lane Kiffin hasn't been shy about bringing NFL rookies back into the fold, as another former Ole Miss star is expected to join LSU
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's not often that teams can add a standout veteran to their roster less than two weeks before the start of the season, but that's exactly what LSU has done twice in the last week. Sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that former Ole Miss star defensive lineman Zxavian Harris is expected to land with the Tigers after a brief stint with the New Orleans Saints.Harris is taking advantage of a recent Louisiana ruling, under which athletes from the Class of 2022 have received temporary restraining orders to gain a fifth year of eligibility. LSU has already made plans to add tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who seems destined for a return to college football after being waived by the Cleveland Browns.Most recently, Harris was in training camp with the Saints after going undrafted in 2026. The Saints waived Harris on Aug. 8, and he hasn't landed with another NFL team, so it is expected that he will reunite with his former head coach in Baton Rouge.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin's pursuit of ex-NFL TE Dae'Quan Wright is latest example of LSU coach not caring what you think
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
A four-star recruit in the 2022 signing class, Harris really broke out as a senior last fall. He was a key cog in the Rebels' defense -- wreaking havoc in the middle of the line to the tune of 58 tackles, 9.0 tackles for loss and 3.0 sacks. That was enough to get Harris invited to the NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis.
Throughout his college career, Harris has appeared in 52 games, and he's accumulated 123 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks. Interior defensive line was going to be a question mark for LSU in 2026, but they may have just found a big answer with Harris.LSU addresses a big needThroughout the offseason, LSU was viewed as a legitimate College Football Playoff contender, mainly because the Tigers boast what might be the most expensive roster in the sport.Kiffin and his staff have spared no expense in hopes of an instant turnaround, but that doesn't mean the roster is flawless. Prior to the addition of Harris, there were some questions in the middle of the defensive line. The Tigers return just 31% of their snaps on the defensive line from last year, which ranks 79th in the country.
Freshmen Deuce Geralds and Richard Anderson -- both highly-touted players -- were expected to factor heavily into that rotation. Talented as they may be, leaning on a freshmen in the trenches can be a gamble in the SEC.Coming out of spring practice, Blake Ruffino of 247Sports told the "Cover 3 Podcast" that the LSU defensive line was a big question mark after watching it get pushed around by the offensive line at times."It gets to a point where, those last two weeks, it was at will," Ruffino said. "I do worry about that defensive line. Now, [five-star defensive lineman] Lamar Brown wasn't there, but my same thought is, 'Are you about to start three true freshmen in the interior of that defensive line?' Yes, it is a concern for me."The Tigers also need a lot from transfers Malik Blocton (Auburn) and Stephiylan Green (Clemson). Both had experience from their previous spots, but neither player posted eye-popping production.
Now, LSU has proven talent and experience at the defensive tackle position with Harris. The Tigers' depth at that spot now looks much more formidable, which is good because they're playing three of Blake Brockermeyer's top 10 offensive lines this fall.Have Harris and Kiffin mended fences?When Kiffin left Oxford for Baton Rouge before the College Football Playoff, he wasn't the most popular man in the Ole Miss locker room. You can certainly count Harris among the players who didn't appreciate the way Kiffin handled things.At the time, Harris told Chris Low that Kiffin taking the LSU job was "like a slap in the face and then a backhand. We took that personally."
Prior to the Rebels' Fiesta Bowl loss to Miami, there was speculation that Kiffin was trying to join the broadcast, but he ultimately attended an LSU women's basketball game. Harris didn't shy away from blasting Kiffin for attempting to steal the team's limelight after jumping ship."That's what Kiffin tried to do," Harris told Low. "He tried to be a damn announcer … trying to be a troll. We were going to troll him. We got something for him. He was just trying to steal our shine. That's all he tried to do. That's all he's been trying to do, is steal our shine."Apparently, that's all water under the bridge with Harris and Kiffin set to join forces yet again. Another payday and the chance to win a national championship can have that effect on players and coaches.
In the world of modern college football, it's probably best not to burn any bridges because things can change very quickly in an unpredictable landscape.

title: Lane Kiffin isn't worried about criticism over LSU's pursuit of Dae'Quan Wright - CBS Sports
description: Wright became the NFL's first active player to enter college football's transfer portal last week
body:
Wright became the NFL's first active player to enter college football's transfer portal last week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Lane Kiffin does not care about pearl-clutching from media members or fellow coaches. His job at LSU is to acquire talent, win football games and hunt championships, and his pursuit of Cleveland Browns tight end and former Ole Miss standout Dae'Quan Wright is another reminder that few coaches navigate college football's lawless landscape better.Call him shameless. Call him calculated. Call him a filthy recruiter. Kiffin will probably retweet the criticism and keep working.Wright's decision to enter the transfer portal after reaching the NFL would have sounded absurd not long ago. Now, amid courtroom victories, temporary restraining orders and eligibility rulings that continue to erase the sport's old boundaries, it represents another opportunity. Kiffin is not responsible for cleaning up the NCAA's mess. He is responsible for building LSU's roster, and if the rules — or a judge — allow him to pursue an NFL player, he likely sees it as negligent not to make the call."Because of the rulings, they are going to play for you or someone else," Kiffin said Monday. "We made the decision to recruit them. It's wrong to be critical of these kids. They were granted a fifth year and a judge said they were wronged."
That is the uncomfortable truth for Kiffin's critics. He is not breaking the system. He is reading it faster than everyone else.And that doesn't mean they have to like it.Lane Kiffin isn't changing; college football is"It used to be once you had an agent or once you went and did the combine," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said. "All those things qualified as you were no longer an amateur. You're a professional now, once you declare for the draft. So to let any of those players come back, fair or unfair to them, it's unfair to the sport, and I think it's unfair to the players that are on current teams for those guys to be coming back."College football's new era rewards aggression, creativity and a willingness to explore every available loophole. Kiffin has never needed permission to push the envelope. 
At LSU, with championship expectations and every resource imaginable, he is simply doing what he does best: winning the transaction."I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago; now I know," Browns coach Todd Monken said over the weekend. "I mean, shit, I didn't know. Now I know. I didn't call him back; I guess I should've."Critics see a broken system; Kiffin sees available talentOutrage has never altered Kiffin's approach. If Wright is legally permitted to return to college and the NCAA cannot stop it, Kiffin sees an available player who could improve LSU's roster. Nothing more.
Recruiting a player from his former program after that player already reached the NFL feels especially brazen, even by Kiffin's standards. It also reinforces every negative perception attached to his Ole Miss exit.Still, Kiffin's responsibility is to win at LSU, not satisfy a national morality test. In this era, restraint earns applause. Aggression acquires talent — and Kiffin knows that, not that he cares about outside opinion."NFL players should not be allowed to go back to play college football.  It's gross negligence," former Heisman winner Robert Griffin III wrote on social media. "It's a disservice to the current college players on any roster.  Any coach or school who allows it should be ashamed of themselves."
And Wright's not the only former college player the Tigers are looking to add before the start of the 2026 season.LSU embracing the eligibility chaosLSU also recently landed a commitment from former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, who made seven starts over four seasons with the Fighting Irish. Tuihalamaka was granted another season of eligibility as part of the Louisiana court ruling for Class of 2022 athletes.Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman wanted no part of an unexpected late addition."For us at Notre Dame, it's just too late [with] the graduate admissions process, and I don't think it would put a person in a good situation this late -- school starts on Monday -- to have success in the classroom and on the field, so that's been our stance on it," Freeman said Friday. "Our admissions has already done their admissions and cycles. That's where the university and the athletic program stand right now."
Kiffin has never cared about his naysayers, especially after messy exits at Tennessee and Ole Miss. And he certainly is not going to start now because college football's latest eligibility twist has people screaming that the sport has become a joke.The process is slimy, and many are calling the sport broken, but Kiffin has heard worse throughout a career spent testing boundaries and irritating traditionalists. He has repeatedly made clear that national perception does not drive his decisions.Kiffin's critics are concerned about what college football has become. LSU's coach is focused on winning within it. In this no-holds-barred era, yelling at your smartphone does not secure championships. Talent does.
